subject: MAP: simulation suite + token-cost gap checks
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@olivehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olive Health Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: initial econ inputs + simulation access request

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency and the fallback behavior. Procurement asked us to lock down the MAP economics and two things came up that I want to confirm as we draft the MAP:

1) We need a small simulation run of our traffic (attached CSV) to validate tokens/$ assumptions across peak and steady state.
2) A crisp checklist of what your team needs from our side (SLA targets, peak QPS, retention needs) so procurement can align docs and timeline.

High level traffic: 150k MAUs for pilot, expected peak concurrency 220 QPS, average session ~3.8 requests, median prompt length 480 tokens, median model response 130 tokens. We flagged caching and batching assumptions in our internal notes and want Redwood's recommended baseline for MAP.

Can you run a sensitivity suite (low/med/high traffic + caching hit 0/10/25%) and return a 3-scenario units-per-dollar snapshot? We have a soft close target of end of June; procurement will need the numbers by 6/10 to get DocuSign routing started.

Thanks,
Maya

Maya Singh
Head of Platform Integrations, Olive Health

Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: initial econ inputs + simulation access request

Maya — thanks for the sample traffic and the timeline. We can absolutely run the sims and will return a concise units-per-dollar table for the MAP. Quick notes and what we need from you to make the numbers defensible: 

What we ran quickly from the CSV (sanity-check numbers):
- Avg tokens per request (prompt + response): 610 tokens (prompt 480 + response 130)
- Avg requests per session: 3.8
- Tokens per MAU (monthly) ~ 610 * 3.8 * peak-active-factor; baseline estimate ~ 8.6M tokens/user/month for active users (we'll refine).

Redwood baseline assumptions we'll use for the 3 scenarios (low/med/high):
- Model variant: rwd-medium-v2 (FP16 equivalent)
- Baseline batching: 1.6x effective batching at 95th pct (continuous batching enables this)
- KV/prefix caching: 0% / 10% / 25% hit rates for the scenarios you asked
- Quantization profile: int8-compat (safe for throughput; we model a ~18% cost reduction vs FP16)
- Network/egress latency budget: 120ms p50 target on dedicated tier; note that higher batching increases latency tail.

Immediate asks from Olive to include in the MAP so procurement can sign off:
- Confirm target SLA (p50/p95 latency SLOs) and allowable latency tradeoffs during peak.
- Confirm whether user data needs to be retained for >30 days (affects cache TTL and storage costs).
- Any requirement for on-prem/Private deployment during pilot (affects reserved capacity pricing).

Plan:
- We will run the three sims and return a one-page units-per-$ table by EOD 6/6 (PST). That includes token counts, estimated token-processing cost, and 3 sensitivity points for caching.
- Karthik will add a short appendix showing effect of 2x batching vs no batching and quantization delta.

Attaching a short checklist and the CSV we used for traceability. Let me know if procurement needs the numbers in a specific format.

Thanks — Priya

Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales (West) | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: initial econ inputs + simulation access request

Priya / team — I ran the first-pass sims with the attached params and am dropping the high-level deltas here so procurement has something actionable quickly. Numbers are illustrative (rounded).

Assumptions used in sims:
- Model token price baseline: $20 per 1M tokens (hosted rwd-medium-v2, pre-commit discounts not applied)
- Quantization delta: -18% unit cost (int8 path)
- Batching impact: 1.0x (no batch) => baseline; 1.6x effective batching => ~30% token-processing cost reduction after pipeline amortization; 2.4x => ~45% reduction but note the latency tail increases significantly.
- Caching: 0% hit => no savings; 10% hit => linear reduction in generated tokens only; 25% => substantial generated-token reduction but prompt tokens often still present.

Snapshot (per-month for pilot, aggregated):
- Low (steady): 20% of expected peak traffic, caching 25%: ~1.1B tokens/month => ~$22k/month base => effective $/MAU ~$0.15 (after quantization & batch uplift).
- Mid (expected): 60% of peak, caching 10%: ~3.6B tokens/month => ~$64k/month => $/MAU ~$0.42.
- High (peak): 100% peak, caching 0%: ~6.0B tokens/month => ~$120k/month => $/MAU ~$0.70.

Key callouts:
- Batching sensitivity: moving from 1.0x to 1.6x yields ~30% cost drop in these sims; moving to 2.4x yields diminishing returns for cost but latency may breach p95 targets.
- Cache semantics: prefix caching (short-term) reduces generated tokens proportionally; full session reuse is rare for your traffic profile so plan conservatively.
- Reserve vs burst: If Olive wants predictable $$, Reserved Dedicated capacity with a small buffer is recommended — we can show Reserved vs Pay-as-you-go delta for the MAP.

Next steps:
- I'll export the sim CSV outputs and a compact one-page chart for your procurement.
- Priya: propose a MAP milestone: 6/10 internal sign-off (numbers accepted) -> 6/18 docuSign routing -> 6/30 target start. If Olive needs earlier, we can compress but need procurement commitment.

Karthik
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priya / Karthik — this is super helpful. Procurement confirmed they can accept the mid-scenario as the basis for negotiating reserved capacity terms, but they asked for the following to finalize: 

1) A sensitivity table that shows mid +/- 20% on QPS and separate rows for 0/10/25% cache hit.
2) An explicit latency vs batching tradeoff summary we can attach to the SLA appendix (p50/p95 numbers).
3) A short blurb on how fallback/model-variant switching will affect costs in the MAP (e.g., if you fallback from rwd-medium-v2 to rwd-small-v2 during heavy tail).

If you can get those to us by the morning of 6/10 we'll route the internal sign-off and start the DocuSign flow. Also please add the Reserved vs PAYG numbers as a single-line delta so procurement can see the committed discount tradeoff.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Maya

Maya Singh
Head of Platform Integrations, Olive Health
